messages:
oncall-bot: ALERT: multi-region failover monitor (failover-health:eu-west) fired. region eu-west-1 p50 latency > 2s and p50 5xx rate > 7% for 3m. paging oncall.
Jamie L: Received. Pulling up multi-region dashboard now. Any recent config pushes?
infra-bot: Deploy bot: No service deploys in the last 15m. LB-config pushed 10m ago to lb-proxy-eu-west (change-id: cfg-2026-03-14-17).
Ravi K: I see a traffic imbalance — eu-west got a spike due to regional preference fallback from ap-southeast after a transient outage there. That influx caused increased KV cache churn on the eu-west runtime pool.
Sana M: Observing a pattern: hosts with highest long-seq proportion show increased GC pauses and 503s from runtime-alloc.
Jamie L: Can someone mute duplicate pages for this alert? It's noisy while we triage. Propose increasing alert "for" to 6m and add fingerprint dedupe for 4m.
Ravi K: Agreed. I'll update the alert rule. Also start a temporary traffic dampening: reduce routing weight for eu-west long-seq by 30%. ops-bot: executing traffic adjust.
ops-bot: traffic-adjust executed: decreased long-seq weight to eu-west by 30% (applied to model-family: *-xlarge).
infra-bot: LB config rollback queued for lb-proxy-eu-west (cfg-2026-03-14-17 -> cfg-2026-03-14-16). ETA ~8m.
Jamie L: While rollback runs, can we add a short-term cache-size bump for the most-impacted workers? Is that safe?
Sana M: We can bump kv_cache_max from 2GB -> 3GB on the three hot workers. Applying now.
infra-bot: kv_cache_max updated on hosts euw2-07, euw2-08, euw2-09.
Ravi K: After cache bump and traffic shift, p50 latency down to 1.1s on eu-west hosts, 5xx rate falling to 1.8%. Good signal.
Jamie L: Rollback of LB config completed. Confirming backend weights restored.
Sana M: Noted customers impacted: two medium customers using long-seq features saw elevated failures, we've posted a status update and DM'd their SEs. status-bot: Status update posted: "Temporary degradation in eu-west; auto-mitigation in progress. No data loss."
Jamie L: Alert tuning proposal for post-incident: 1) region failover rule: change from absolute 5xx rate > 5% to p95-based window for long-seq traffic; 2) add dedupe fingerprinting on failover monitor alerts; 3) add multi-region token-length heatmap to the SRE dashboard.
Ravi K: I'll open FUPs and attach PromQL examples. Quick PromQL for long-seq p95 failure fraction we used: ```histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{tokens_count_bucket=~">1024"}[5m])) by (le, region))```
Sana M: Also recommend adding a preflight check for LB config pushes that simulates traffic distribution changes and flags >15% backend weight tilt.
Jamie L: Creating follow-ups: FUP-700 (dashboard heatmap + per-region token metrics), FUP-701 (alert tuning + dedupe), FUP-702 (LB preflight check).
ops-bot: Created tickets: FUP-700, FUP-701, FUP-702 (assigned to eng-sre and eng-runtime).
Ravi K: I'll draft a short runbook addition for handling long-seq-induced cache pressure and include the quick traffic-adjust commands: ```# shift long seq traffic away from eu-west
redwoodctl traffic route --model-family "*-xlarge" --from-region eu-west --to-region eu-central --weight 30
```
Jamie L: Handoff: Sana, can you take the 45m watch and triage follow-ups? I'll update the incident ticket timeline and prepare a short post-incident note.
Sana M: Taking watch. I'll also collect per-host GC traces and attach to FUP-701.
Jamie L: Post-incident summary (brief): root cause: sudden regional fallback traffic + LB config change produced concentrated long-seq load -> kv cache churn and GC pauses on eu-west workers; mitigation: traffic dampening (30% long-seq away), kv_cache bump on three hosts, LB rollback; alerting changes: increase alert "for" to 6m temporarily and add fingerprint dedupe; follow-ups created.
status-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring.
Sana M: Logged an action item: add p95 long-seq failure metric to nightly alerts to catch degradations earlier (added to FUP-701).
Ravi K: Final checks: eu-west p50 latency 0.9s, 5xx rate 0.2%. Marking as mitigated unless new spikes occur.
Jamie L: Thanks all. I'll file a short postmortem draft and schedule a follow-up review with LB and runtime teams next week. :thumbsup:
Sana M: Will escalate if anything pops in the watch window.
